questions.stem: According to Newton's First Law, what happens to an object when the resultant force acting on it is zero?

options.text: It remains at rest or continues moving at constant velocity
It accelerates in the direction of its motion

questions.explanation: Newton's First Law states that an object will remain at rest or continue to move at constant velocity (in a straight line) unless acted upon by a resultant force. Zero resultant force means no change in velocity.

questions.stem: A book is sitting on a table. What forces act on it, and why doesn't it move?

options.text: Only gravity acts on it, but the table blocks it
Weight acts downward and the normal reaction force acts upward -- they are balanced
No forces act on it because it is stationary
Friction prevents it from falling through the table

questions.explanation: The book has two forces acting on it: its weight pulling it downward and the normal reaction force from the table pushing it upward. These forces are balanced (equal and opposite), so the resultant force is zero and the book stays at rest.
